findings.text: non-blocking: the 'if pointers is None: return _ReviewInFlightIndex(())' branch is unreachable, because the function's only call site is line 757 and it passes the already-resolved candidates list, never None; the docstring's claim that a caller with no snapshot "is handed an index of its own for the one call that asked" therefore rests on no executed code. What actually keeps a caller outside a tick reading live is that list_live returns a fresh list per call, so the id-key misses and a new index is built - the guarantee is incidental to the cache key rather than made by the branch it is documented in.

non-blocking: the per-snapshot index is shared between the calls of one live-pointer read only through the module-global _REVIEW_INDEX_CACHE keyed on id(pointers), capped at _REVIEW_INDEX_LIMIT = 4 entries, and the measured linearity is single-threaded. With five or more distinct snapshot objects live at once - the station tick plus the session sweeps that duties are derived off the tick thread, plus the obligations pass through the recovery alias - the entries evict each other and every classified run rebuilds the index it walks, returning the walk toward the base cost it was written to remove from a code path that looks unchanged. A pass held by the caller (a context, as review_heads_resolve_once already holds one in this module) would not depend on how many readers are in flight.

non-blocking: _CheckCounter._record counts only while the counter's own depth is armed, and _counted_lookup (line 186) arms it around exactly two names, _review_pointer_rubric and _review_subject. The budget assertion therefore cannot see a per-candidate filesystem read reintroduced anywhere else in _review_in_flight's loop body (line 751-766) or in the helpers it calls there, so a regression that relocated the sweep rather than restoring it would leave the count at 2.00 per pointer and both cases green. The two armed readers are where the base cost lived, which is why the reinstated-base negative control reddens; the guard is narrower than the property it is cited for.

non-blocking: _ReviewInFlightIndex is a second per-pass memo in a module that already owns one - review_heads_resolve_once at line 1006 with the ContextVar _REVIEW_HEAD_REGION, whose comment at line 1149 states the same rule this class's docstring restates ('the first reader in a region resolves it and the rest are answered from the result'; 'outside a region each call resolves on its own'). The addition does not extend or wrap that owner: it caches a different answer set (record directory, declared record names, composed names, review subject) under a different lifetime rule, the identity of a caller-supplied sequence in a global four-entry LRU, so the offsetting defect the region's comment guards against is answered twice in one file by two mechanisms with two rules.

non-blocking: the fragment states that 'counting every existence check the whole classification pass made at the base revision, the same fixture cost 73,601 checks - 368 per pointer' as a measurement, but no log under the run directory carries that reading: logs/ holds gate-head.log (head, scoped, 400), negative-control.log (mutated tree, scoped, 60,960 and 243,520), the two suite arms and the two importer arms, and a grep for 73601 over logs/ and arms/ finds nothing. The instrument's liveness is already shown by the recorded negative control, so the number is decorative, but a figure a reader cannot open should not be presented beside the ones they can.

justifications.reuse: the closest owner of 'answer each per-pass derived read once and derive it freshly outside the pass' is review_heads_resolve_once at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1006 with _REVIEW_HEAD_REGION at :1151, and the class added at :364 caches a different answer set under a different lifetime rule rather than extending or wrapping that owner; the search over reckon/crew found no shared per-pass memo other than that region; so the addition is a second mechanism for the same purpose rather than a duplicate of an owned function.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three paths in the diff - reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py, tests/test_a_review_lookup_is_linear.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once/a-review-lookup-is-linear.html - are every one of them inside the fence the source manifest declares, and the keyword-only index argument at :595 has its only caller at :759, so the signature change reaches no test or other module.
